attractions.name: Manchar Lake
attractions.description: One of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, home to diverse birdlife and traditional fishing communities living on houseboats.

attractions.name: Johi & Khirthar National Park (day trip)
attractions.description: A large national park in the Khirthar mountain range, home to wild sheep, ibex, and rugged desert-mountain scenery.

food_places.name: Manchar Lake fish restaurants
food_places.specialty: Fresh lake fish, a local specialty

weather_info.climate_type: Hot desert climate, very hot summers

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild, 12-25°C, best time for birdwatching at Manchar Lake

travel_tips.tip: Dadu is a convenient base for visiting both Manchar Lake and Khirthar National Park in the same trip.
Hire a local taxi for the Manchar Lake trip, and consider a boat ride once there to see the floating fishing communities.
Carry water and sun protection given the very high summer temperatures in this region.
Visit Manchar Lake in winter for the best birdwatching, when migratory birds are present in large numbers.

history.founded: An old settlement along the Indus River plains, with the district taking on administrative importance in the British era
history.city_history: Dadu developed as a district center serving the surrounding agricultural areas along the Indus, and is best known today as the gateway to Manchar Lake, one of Asia's largest freshwater lakes and an important habitat for migratory birds.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
